criterion: Identifies Store 18 — Memphis and compares Easter Sunday, March 31, 2024 with Sunday, March 24, 2024.
Quantifies payment net sales as approximately $1,101.20 versus $5,535.91, a decline of about $4,434.71 or 80.1%; gross profit fell from about $3,141.26 to $604.74, about 80.8%.
Identifies transaction and unit volume as the leading observed driver: transactions fell from 67 to 12, about 82.1%, and units from 145 to 23, about 84.1%.
Rules out basket deterioration as the main cause because average payment net basket increased from about $82.63 to $91.77, about 11.1%.
Rules out a discount-led decline or a straightforward discount remedy: discount rate fell from about 5.17% to 1.41%, and discount dollars fell from about $301.59 to $15.80.
Uses Easter Sunday and chain results as appropriate context. Chain payment net sales fell from about $74,763.40 to $22,317.74, about 70.1%, supporting a broad holiday traffic effect.
Does not claim a complete closure, data loss, or zero sales: the target store recorded 12 payment transactions and $1,101.20 in payment net sales.
Recommends an operational or planning response—such as holiday staffing, hours, inventory, or demand forecasting—with a next-holiday validation check rather than a reflexive price promotion.
